subsystems.name: Neural culture
subsystems.role: the living processor — a network of neurons grown in the lab.

subsystems.name: Electrode interface
subsystems.role: translates between the biological and electronic domains.

subsystems.name: Life-support system
subsystems.role: keeps the neurons alive and stable for weeks to months.
parts: microfluidic perfusion for fresh medium and waste removal

subsystems.name: Stimulation and recording electronics
subsystems.role: applies patterned electrical stimuli and captures the neurons' electrical activity.

subsystems.name: Closed-loop computing stack
subsystems.role: decodes neural activity into outputs and feeds inputs back in real time.

subsystems.name: Containment and safety
subsystems.role: ensures biological material stays contained and the system is safe to operate.

buildSteps.title: Prepare the substrate
buildSteps.detail: A multi-electrode array or CMOS chip is cleaned and coated with adhesion molecules such as poly-D-lysine or laminin so neurons can attach.

buildSteps.title: Culture the neurons
buildSteps.detail: Stem cells are differentiated into neurons or primary tissue is dissociated; the cells are plated onto the electrode array at controlled density.

buildSteps.title: Maintain the culture
buildSteps.detail: The array is kept in a 37 °C incubator and perfused with nutrient medium; the neurons spontaneously form a connected network within days.

buildSteps.title: Connect the electronics
buildSteps.detail: The electrodes are wired to amplifiers and stimulators that can both listen to and talk to the network.

buildSteps.title: Characterise the network
buildSteps.detail: Baseline activity is recorded; researchers map which electrodes see which patterns and how the network responds to simple stimuli.

buildSteps.title: Close the loop
buildSteps.detail: A computer translates recorded spikes into a task output and generates patterned stimuli as feedback, letting the culture learn through plasticity.

buildSteps.title: Scale and stabilise
buildSteps.detail: More electrodes, higher neuron densities, or three-dimensional organoid cultures are used to increase computing capacity and longevity.

buildSteps.title: Package for use
buildSteps.detail: The living core is encapsulated with fluidics and electronics into a robust module that can run for weeks without manual intervention.

prerequisites.why: provides the living processor and the ability to grow reproducible networks.

prerequisites.tech: Multi-electrode arrays and CMOS microelectrode chips
prerequisites.why: enable non-destructive stimulation and recording from hundreds to thousands of neurons.

prerequisites.tech: Real-time signal processing and machine learning
prerequisites.why: decodes neural activity and closes the feedback loop fast enough for learning.
networks currently survive for weeks to months; commercial use would need months to years.

prerequisites.tech: Understanding of neural coding and plasticity
prerequisites.why: we can train simple behaviours but do not yet reliably program complex computations.

pathway.milestone: lab demonstrations where cultured neurons learn simple tasks such as playing Pong
pathway.unlocks: proof that biological networks can act as adaptive processors in a closed loop.

pathway.milestone: more complex tasks and longer-lived cultures, including three-dimensional organoids
pathway.unlocks: higher capacity and stability for practical pattern recognition.

pathway.milestone: hybrid systems where a biological core handles low-power sensing and a silicon chip handles logic
pathway.unlocks: ultra-low-power edge computing for specialised tasks.

pathway.milestone: standardised, reliable biological processors with defined interfaces
pathway.unlocks: commercial use in AI and robotics — if ethical and biosecurity hurdles are cleared.
